decision_log: - pass-3-q3: bruit & fame → "rumour and common repute", bruit & renommée → "rumour and renown" wherever either pair recurs; the §9 seed row, annot-041, annot-053, annot-062 and texte-62 already read so, annot-002 had the two swapped and annot-060 dropped "common"; sections touched: annot-002, annot-060

- pass-3-q3: Et de dire que … → "And as to saying that …" (the record's formula for taking up the appellant's point, texte-56, texte-58, texte-62); the literal majority form, texte-62's "as to the argument that" brought in line; sections touched: texte-62
- pass-3-q3: ſainctement → "holily" (annot-062, annot-083); Coras's word is religious and annot-083 already had it, annot-062's "wisely" lost the colour; sections touched: annot-062
- pass-3-q3: Ioinct que / ioint que → "Added to which" (texte-58, texte-66); one English for the record's formula introducing a further ground; sections touched: texte-58

findings.note: Ringold–Lewis agree in substance. Note the sentence runs on into texte-57 (*Ny fait rien auſsi*), as the English does.
R&L: "in addition to denying that the prisoner is not Martin Guerre" — misreads *ioint que la negation qu'ils font … vient aiſéement en preuue* (the negation comes easily into proof). Ours is right.

R&L: "far from being a thousand" for *encor qu'ils fuſſent mille* (even though they were a thousand). Ours is right. Also *goutes de ſang* is plural here where texte-40 had the singular; kept as printed in each place.
R&L: "broken teeth" for *ſoubre-dents*; the word is *surdents*, supernumerary teeth (pass-2 decision). Ours is right; the same divergence stands at texte-40.

R&L read *perſonnément* as "personally", which matches the attested Middle French adverb; our main reading now agrees and the [unclear] flag is kept because a misprint for *pertinemment* remains possible. R&L otherwise agree (the confession at the execution, the likeness of the sisters).

*luy eſtant en preuention de meſme faict deuant le Seneſchal* — both we ("for the same deed") and R&L ("for the same reason") read it literally, but texte-47 says the Seneschal's prosecution was on other charges (*d'autres cas*). Coras's own inconsistency; left as printed, worth a note in the apparatus.

R&L: "holding him in legal custody under the palace guard" for *luy tenant l'arreſt clos chez la garde du palais*; same meaning as our "close arrest", which follows the pass-0 decision on the second sense of *arrest*. R&L "reported by the soldier" for *conſigné* is interpretive; ours keeps *consigner* → set down (texte-21).

R&L: "being sworn, gave answers" for *conſigne, & baille enſeignes*; *conſigner* is "to set down" (texte-21), not "to swear". Ours is right. R&L's "a liar, a troublemaker, a good-for-nothing" for *affronteur, meſchant, beliſtre* differs in wording only; ours follows the §9 rows.
R&L: "the justices" for *les commiſſaires*; ours keeps "commissioners" (§9, annot-021). Otherwise agree.
R&L agree ("by no multiplication of penalties, summonses or orders"). The subject of *exhibez* is supplied in both translations; ours now brackets it.

*& confeſſe frãchement l'erreur … m'auoit* — *confeſſe* may be third person ("she confesses", so R&L "frankly confessed") or the start of direct speech (ours, which the first-person *m'auoit* then requires). Interpretive; left.
R&L: "through imprudence augmented by the seductions" for *par imprudence, & ſurmontee des ſeductions* (overcome by). Ours is right.

R&L agree that *demeuroit par l'appel encor arreſtée* is detention ("she remained in detention throughout the appeal"), the second sense of *arrest* settled in §12. R&L "by verdict of the judge at Rieux" for *par ſentence du Iuge de Rieux*: ours keeps "judgment" per §5.

R&L divergences in the decision, all theirs: "the appeal … has been granted, performed and nullified" garbles the formula *a mis, & met l'appellation … & ce dont a eſté appelé, au neant* (set aside as null, §5); "the Court" for *à Iuſtice* (ours: "of Justice"); "executioner of the High Court" for *executeur de la haute Iuſtice* (high justice, not the court); "Legally pronounced" for *Prononce iudicialement*. R&L do not translate the display head EXPOSITION DES Paroles de l'arreſt or the one-word TEXTE heads (texte-81–84).

Coras writes *le priſonnier* for the man brought from the Basque country at two, i.e. Martin Guerre, not du Tilh; translated as printed. *diſertement* is "distinctly" here (an infant's articulation) against §9's "eloquently" at annot-108; the contexts differ and both stand.

Note {b} (*l. ſancimus. C. de pœn.*) has no marker in the French prose; the English matches the French sequence and cannot add one. *la perſonne qui veut punir* is translated as the passive ("whom one wishes to punish"), which the sense requires; the reading is logged to misreadings-pass-3-q3.

Note {c} (*l actor C. de proba. …*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches. *ce premier iour d'octobre 1560* is Coras dating his own writing, and corroborates §1's "first draft finished by 1 October 1560".
Note {g} (*Panorme & les autre au c. præterea*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches.

Note {g} (*Iaques Butrigaire*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches. *bien qne l'vn d'eux depoſent d'vne eſpece d'hereſies, diſent ils …* is defective in the print (the second witness's clause has dropped); the bracketed supplement "[and the other to another]" is kept.
Note {g} (*Accurſe en la l. iij P. eiuſdé …*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches.
Note {c} (*l. eum qui. D. de probat. …*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches.

*cõme ce faict ici. Apres infinis autres met en euidence deux pauures innocẽs …* — the deed "brings to light" the two innocents; our "makes plain: two poor innocents … who … were delivered" joins the clauses more loosely but keeps the sense. Left.

*attendu qu'elle ne conſiſte point ſeulement en drogues, bruuages, & empoiſonnemens* is rendered "consists in nothing but"; "does not consist only in" is grammatically possible but would invert Coras's argument (Pharmacy is wrongly counted as magic because it is mere drugs, unless a prodigious effect follows). The Faustina [unclear] stays: the print lacks the main verb (Capitolinus has the gladiator killed and Faustina bathed in his blood). *amiable* for *admirable* is logged to misreadings. The heading is misprinted ANNOT. LXVI.; our id annot-071 follows the true count.
*le Pape Iean xiij* — Coras's (Platina's) numbering; the pope slain by a jealous husband is usually counted John XII. Kept as printed, for the Notes.

The verse quotations are presented unevenly: *Illa malis* and *Codrus* carry the Latin in parentheses, the Ovid, Callimachus and Horace passages do not. Presentation only; left for the apparatus pass. *Numantius* writing to Cicero is unidentified (perhaps a garbled correspondent of the *Ad familiares*); kept as printed. *vne perſonne, ſuiette par trop à ſes paſſions* rendered "her passions" since the person is Bertrande; acceptable.
The [unclear] stays: *ceſte eſpece de mort luy ſembloit pour vn ſi prodigieux … proditeur …* has no predicate in the print; "too honourable" is the evident sense and the whole book gives no better.

The [unclear] on the Ulpian sentence stays (*& telle, (diſoit … Vlpien qu'il en ſoit) autres aux exemple*). The French notes carry an unkeyed entry {_} (*ſiue adulterium. x. diſt.*); for the Notes pass.

Note {b} (*l j. P fin. D ad l. Cornel. de falſ.*) has no marker in the French prose; English matches. Coras's "Herod Antipas" (for Herod the Great, father of Alexander) and "Cambyses king of the Assyrians" are his own errors and are kept; *l'an mille 225* is kept literal ("one thousand 225").
Cross-reference n. b *En l'annotation lxiij* points to the Pompeius Strabo and cook story, which is annot-063 in the true count; nothing to change.
